VPT Mechanical Solutions
Kalgoorlie-Boulder, WA 6430
Full-time | Permanent

Salary: $80,000 – $85,000 per annum plus superannuation

About the Role

VPT Mechanical Solutions is seeking a skilled and reliable Fire Protection Equipment Technician to join our team in Kalgoorlie-Boulder, Western Australia. This full-time position is responsible for the installation, inspection, testing, servicing, maintenance, and repair of fire protection equipment and systems to ensure compliance with Australian Standards and workplace safety requirements.

Key Responsibilities
Install, inspect, test, service, and maintain a range of fire protection equipment and systems.
Carry out routine inspections and scheduled maintenance of fire extinguishers, hose reels, hydrants, fire blankets, and emergency exit lighting.
Install, inspect, and maintain fire and smoke doors, passive fire and smoke containment systems, and associated equipment.
Service and test gaseous fire suppression systems and foam generation equipment in accordance with relevant standards.
Identify faults and undertake repairs or replacement of defective fire protection equipment and components.
Perform functional testing to ensure fire protection systems operate safely and effectively.
Complete inspection reports, maintenance records, and compliance documentation accurately.
Ensure all work is performed in accordance with Australian Standards, relevant legislation, and workplace health and safety procedures.
Liaise professionally with clients and provide recommendations for required repairs or system upgrades.
Maintain tools, equipment, and service vehicles in a safe and operational condition.
Skills, Qualifications and Experience

To be considered for this position, applicants must meet one of the following:

Hold an AQF Certificate III (or equivalent qualification) relevant to Fire Protection, Fire Systems, Mechanical Services, or a related trade; or
Have at least three (3) years of full-time relevant work experience as a Fire Protection Equipment Technician or in a similar role.

The successful applicant will also demonstrate:

Experience installing, testing, and maintaining fire protection equipment and systems.
Knowledge of Australian Standards relating to fire protection systems and equipment.
Strong fault-finding and problem-solving skills.
Ability to read technical drawings, service manuals, and maintenance schedules.
Excellent attention to detail and commitment to quality workmanship.
Good communication and customer service skills.
Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
A strong commitment to workplace health and safety.
Registration or licensing (where required) and a current driver's licence are desirable.
What We Offer
Full-time permanent employment.
Competitive annual salary of $80,000 – $85,000 plus superannuation.
Supportive and professional working environment.
Ongoing training and career development opportunities.
Long-term employment with an established and growing company.

Temporary Full Time position working up to 31 January 2027, across a rotating 7 day, 24 hour roster

Overview

Port Lincoln Hospital is the cornerstone of healthcare across the Eyre Peninsula, and the team behind the front desk is just as important as the clinical staff on the floor. If you're an experienced healthcare administrator ready to step into a leadership role, this short-term contract offers a genuine opportunity to make your mark at the heart of Eyre and Far North Local Health Network.

What You'll Be Leading

Reporting to the Manager of Patient Services, you'll oversee the day-to-day delivery of administrative and patient services across Port Lincoln Hospital. This is a hands-on leadership role operating across a 24-7 roster environment, with a contract end date of 31 January 2027.

Lead, supervise, and allocate work to patient services staff, ensuring consistent and timely service delivery

Oversee patient record management including creation, storage, retention, and disposal of medical and general records in line with policy

Manage Freedom of Information requests and human resource administration duties

Maintain a professional reception function, ensuring patients and visitors receive a respectful and efficient experience

What You'll Bring

Demonstrated experience in a supervisory or team leadership role within a healthcare or health administration setting

Sound knowledge of patient information systems and medical records management

Familiarity with SA Health or public health sector administrative frameworks, policies, and compliance requirements

Proven ability to coordinate rosters and manage workload allocation across a team

Strong interpersonal skills with a commitment to patient-centred service

Availability and willingness to work across a 24-hour, 7-day roster

Ready to Apply?

Submit your application via the SA Health careers portal, including a current CV and a cover letter addressing the key responsibilities outlined above. For a confidential discussion about the role, reach out to the hiring manager through the contact details listed on the advertisement. Applications are reviewed as received, so don't wait to put yours forward.

About Us

With its ancient outback landscapes, boutique vineyards, oyster farms and Australia's best-kept-secret surf coast, Eyre and Far North will inspire and energise you.

The Eyre and Far North Local Health Network (EFNLHN) is responsible for the planning and delivery of hospital and health services over 337,626 square kilometres, taking in the Eyre Peninsula, western part of South Australia and north to Coober Pedy. We are one of the largest LHNs by area in Australia and communities include Ceduna, Cleve, Coober Pedy, Cowell, Cummins, Elliston, Kimba, Oodnadatta, Port Lincoln, Streaky Bay, Tumby Bay and Wudinna.

Services include acute care, medical, accident and emergency, surgery, birthing and midwifery, specialist consultancy, renal dialysis, chemotherapy, transfusions, rehabilitation, residential and community aged care, respite care, transitional care packages, Aboriginal health, mental health, allied health, community health, community nursing, palliative care, community home support packages and home modifications.

Click here to learn more about living and working in Eyre and Far North Local Health Network.

Why Join Us

Make a real difference and feel like an important part of the community. Being part of Eyre & Far North means you will be supported both personally and professionally, can take advantage of education and training opportunities, will have access to flexible working hours and be part of an inter-professional approach to holistic health care.

Salary package a range of benefits (including living expenses such as mortgage, rent, utility bills and groceries) up to $9,010 each FBT year + $2,650 for Meal Entertainment expenses each FBT year Click here more information

Wellbeing and counselling support: support for you and your family via our free Employee Assistance Program

Relocation support: relocation reimbursement of up to $15,000 may be available to people relocating for this opportunity. More information available from SA Health Careers - Relocation support.

Employee recognition: supportive and collaborative work environment where your contributions are valued and recognised.

Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion

SA Health is committed to providing an inclusive workplace that embraces diversity and inclusion for all employees. We strongly encourage applications from people of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander descent, culturally diverse backgrounds, members of the LGBTIQA+SB community and people who live with disability and-or neurodivergence.

We are committed to making workplace adjustments to provide a positive and supportive work environment. You are encouraged to let us know if have any support or access requirements during the recruitment process and beyond to ensure you can perform at your best.

Applicant Information

The South Australian public sector promotes diversity and flexible ways of working part-time. Applicants are encouraged to discuss the flexible working arrangements for this role.

Appointment will be subject to a satisfactory Criminal History Check and appropriate immunisation requirements.

Check(s)

Are you a talented Clinician looking to make a significant impact within regional communities?

About the role:

The Stroke Care Coordinator will be responsible for the implementation, coordination and evaluation of stroke care to the patients of the Stroke Services at Wagga Wagga Base Hospital. 

This includes provision of services to the Acute Stroke Unit, coordination of the patient's care through the acute phase of treatment, and the initiation of, and participation in, stroke education and service development across the Murrumbidgee Local Health District. 

As the Stroke Care Coordinator, you will:

Establish and maintain close working relationships with all relevant personnel including internal and external health provided partners.

Participate in the development and implementation of management strategies within the Stroke Unit.

Participate in the strategic planning process and implementation of the Stroke Services Business plan.

Act as a team leader for Stroke Allied Health team and assist in management of the EEG department.

Facilitate the Multidisciplinary Stroke Team to adapt or modify clinical pathways developed for the management of patients presenting with suspected stroke.

Coordinate and participate in weekly team meetings, case conferences and doctors rounds.Be a referral agent to services and a link between various services with the hospital and the patient.

Maintain an advanced level of expertise in stroke management.

What MLHD offer:

At Murrumbidgee Local Health District (MLHD), we offer more than a job - we offer the chance to make a real difference.

Meaningful Impact - Play a vital role in delivering essential health services to our diverse and vibrant regional communities.

Flexible Working Arrangements - Designed to support work-life balance, aligned with NSW Health policy.

Generous Salary Packaging - Access up to $20,600 per annum tax-free for living expenses, plus the option for novated car leasing.

Professional Development - Take advantage of ongoing learning and career development opportunities.

Health & Wellbeing Support - Benefit from our comprehensive wellness programs for you and your family, including Employee Assistance Programs Fitness Passport and initiatives to support both physical and mental health.

Click here to discover why MLHD is the right place to contribute to healthier communities.

Our ideal candidate will demonstrate:

Relevant Allied Health or Nursing qualification with a minimum five years full time equivalent post graduate experience

Good understanding of stroke care, its management and outcomes.

Ability to initiate, complete and evaluate quality improvement projects, contributing to the National Standards accreditation tool.

Experience in managing and facilitating a successful team environment.

High level of Information technology literacy in Office automation programs (including word processing, e-mail and spreadsheets) 

More information:

 2) Find out more about applying for this position

For role related queries or questions contact Kristy Watson - Operational Nurse Manager on Kristy.Watson@health.nsw.gov.au for a confidential chat.

Daylesford Hotel is a much-loved local pub in the heart of Daylesford. A place where the fire's always on, the beer's cold, and the food is exactly what you want it to be. Pizza is a cornerstone of what we do.

About the Position

We're looking for a Chef de Partie – Pizza. This is a focused role for someone who genuinely loves the craft, from dough management and fermentation through to service execution. You'll be responsible for the consistency and quality of our pizza output in a high-volume, fast-paced environment.

Key Responsibilities:

Own the pizza section end-to-end, from dough preparation and proofing through to service.
Maintain consistent quality in shaping, topping, and cooking across the full menu.
Manage dough fermentation schedules and daily prep in line with service requirements.
Follow kitchen hygiene, WH&S, food safety, and stock management procedures, including rotation and labelling.
Oversee section cleanliness and ensure proper storage and maintenance of ingredients and equipment.
Work collaboratively with the broader kitchen team and support junior staff where required.
About You:

2–3 years of experience in a professional kitchen, with at least 1 year dedicated experience on a pizza section.
Culinary qualification. 
A solid understanding of dough — fermentation, hydration, and how it changes under different conditions.
Ability to maintain quality and pace through a busy service.
Strong organisational skills and attention to detail.
Pride in the section and a no-shortcuts approach to the work.
Daylesford Hotel is managed by Walter Christy Pty Ltd, which also oversees the management of Cliffy's Emporium. While each venue has its own identity, both share a commitment to quality food, great service, and genuine hospitality.

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Monash Health exists to reimagine care, so that people can live their best lives. 






We provide safe and equitable care, for every stage of life, delivered with world-leading expertise and over 175 years of experience. 






As a leading academic health service, we're committed to providing tomorrow's care today by integrating research, teaching and training into everyday practice. 






Our team of 24,000 people are full hearted, open minded and all in. Together, we provide more than 250 integrated services for every stage of life at over 50 locations and in the community across south-east Melbourne, Victoria, serving 1.2 million residents in the South Metro Local Health Service Network. 


Are you currently part of the team at Monash Health? Use your network login to access the Monash Health Careers portal and discover all the job opportunities open to you, to support growing your career within the organisation.




To see first-hand what our colleagues think about working here, take a look at the following short videos monashhealth.org-careers.


Key customer service leadership role 


Deliver an exceptional customer experience to three hospitals in our network


Permanent, full time role, based at Clayton with travel across sites 




About the Role


Oversee the delivery of an outstanding customer experience, every time. 



This is a rare opportunity for an experienced Customer Service professional to lead our patient-facing administrative teams at three of our key locations. Reporting to a skilled, influential Operations Director, you'll be accountable for ensuring your front of house teams deliver a friendly, empathetic and efficient customer experience to everyone who interacts with our health service, whether in person, virtually or by phone. 



In this varied role, your success will be measured across these key result areas:



Operational performance and patient flow


Collaboration and establishment of effective functional business relationships to maximise influence 


Excellence in customer service, in every interaction


Admissions governance and data integrity


Education and capability development


Leadership and change management


Communication and information management




Partnering effectively with a peer Customer Service Manager for other Monash Health sites, this role has accountability for our Customer Service and Admissions functions at Monash Medical Centre, Clayton, Moorabbin Hospital and the Victorian Heart Hospital. Accordingly, travel across Monash Health will be required. While the consumer facing nature of this role requires an on-site presence, we have some flexibility in relation to days and hours of work. 




About You


A natural collaborator, you relish the opportunity to ensure a consistently kind, caring and friendly service is delivered by the teams you lead. Demonstrating "out of the box" thinking and a capacity to innovate, you embrace opportunities to trial new approaches and to manage changes to operating practices when relevant. Above all, you are passionate about making our patients' and visitors' experience the best it can be. 



On a personal level, you are: 



Highly organised


Flexible and able to adapt readily to changing priorities 


A highly effective communicator, with active listening skills


An inspiring leader who brings out the best in your people 




What you need




Demonstrated experience leading a large service delivery team in a complex environment


Proven success in training and developing your people to work to their full potential 


Strong knowledge of health services operations, in particular: 





Admissions policies and procedures


Patient Administration systems (PAS)


Health Information and Patient Services





Demonstrated ability to effectively manage resources, systems and service performance


Current driver's licence




A business or health-related qualification, along with experience in a healthcare, emergency services, aged care or other high risk, regulated environment, are highly desirable.



Benefits of working at Monash Health




Monash Health offers a range of benefits, including: 



Comprehensive employee health and wellbeing programs including Fitness Passport


Five weeks annual leave with leave loading


Monthly ADOs for full-time employees 


Salary packaging benefits










For a confidential discussion and to explore this opportunity further, please reach out to Alex Caravelas, Operations Director, Patient Flow and Emergency Management, on 0436 690 795.



Position Description can be found here





Our Culture and Values

Target Business Services

Location: 663 Warringah Road, Forestville NSW 2087
Salary: $100,000 plus 12% superannuation
Position; Full time, Permanent

Our client Patel Traders Pty Ltd as trustee for the J & B Patel Family Trust operates a Metro Petroleum station at Forestville NSW. The client is currently seeking an experienced and dynamic Retail Manager to lead their team and will be responsible for the overall leadership, coordination, and performance of all day-to-day operational functions at the service station. This includes managing the retail fuel forecourt, convenience store, automotive products, vehicle servicing, and convenience items. staff supervision, and compliance with all occupational health, safety and environmental (HSE) standards. 

The role is central to ensuring that the site operates smoothly, delivering high levels of customer service, maintaining inventory and merchandising standards, controlling operational costs, and ensuring the integrity and security of daily financial transactions.

The managerial and administrative aspect of your role will encompass determining product mix, stock levels and service standards, selling goods, maintaining records of stock, financial transactions and ensuring compliance with occupational health and safety regulations.

Key Responsibilities:

-	Store/ Fuel station operations: Manage daily operations, ensuring a well-organized, clean, and welcoming environment.
-	Staff Management: Recruit, train, and supervise store staff, fostering a motivated and productive team.
-	Customer Service: Maintain high service standards, promptly addressing customer inquiries and concerns.
-	Inventory Management: Monitor stock levels, coordinate orders, and ensure optimal product availability. Formulate and implement purchasing strategies and set competitive pricing.
-	Sales & Marketing: Develop and implement strategies to drive sales, including promotions and special offers.
-	Compliance: Ensure adherence to workplace health & safety regulations and company policies.
-	Financial Oversight: Manage budgets, monitor financial transactions, and ensure profitability goals are met.

Minimum Requirements:

-	AQF Associate Degree, Advanced Diploma, or Diploma in a relevant field
-	Minimum one  year of experience in a similar role within the retail sector
-	In the absence of formal qualifications, at least three years of relevant experience may substitute, with additional on-the-job training as necessary. 
-	Proven ability to lead and manage a team in a fast-paced retail environment

Skills & Attributes:

-	Strong leadership and staff management capabilities
-	Excellent verbal and written communication skills
-	Ability to drive sales and achieve business targets
-	Experience in stock management and merchandising
-	Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail

If you are a passionate and experienced retail professional looking for a leadership role, we’d love to hear from you!

To apply for this position, email your resume to recruitment@targetbusiness.com.au  

Please note only shortlisted candidates will be contacted and your application will be treated as strictly confidential.
